appraisal_events.evidence: «Incertain si Ibsen ou d'Annunzio étaient morts ou vivants», he imagines books as «une espèce de cube dont une face est enlevée»; he judges «parfaitement convenable» only the man who writes obituary notices citing his name among mourners, and calls his enemies arrivistes with a misused idiom, «ne sachant pas bien le sens des locutions».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator uses free indirect style to expose the duc's ignorance, his vanity about seeing his name in the paper, and his linguistic incompetence; the ridicule is the narration's own, not merely reported.

appraisal_events.evidence: She walks «entre une double haie d'invités» who, «sachant qu'ils ne connaîtraient jamais "Oriane"», call their wives to look — «Ursule, vite, vite, venez voir Madame de Guermantes» — and would nearly climb on chairs «comme à la revue du 14 juillet ou au Grand Prix».
appraisal_events.explanation: Her standing is displayed and confirmed by the assembled room, which treats her as an unapproachable spectacle; the comedy falls on the gawking guests rather than on her.

appraisal_events.evidence: The duchesse mocks her «grande machine annuelle» and her inability to miss a party; the narration then shows her recruiting «les derniers adhérents» in person and declares her salon «un des derniers» of Paris, «moins recherchés que fuis», its guests coming «en service commandé» and its prestige existing «que pour ceux dont la vie mondaine consiste seulement à lire le compte rendu... dans le Gaulois ou le Figaro».
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage concedes her long labor of transmuting «un salon de lépreux en un salon de grandes dames» only to deny that ascent any real standing, exposing her eminence as an illusion sustained by newspaper readers.

appraisal_events.evidence: Left among strangers and feeling in the way, «prêtes à mourir de froid comme deux hirondelles qui n'ont pas émigré à temps», she is simply not invited the following year; Mme de Franquetot's intercession obtains only «Mais on peut toujours entrer écouter de la musique si ça vous amuse, ça n'a rien de criminel !», and she stays away.
appraisal_events.explanation: A boundary is shown closing on her: after years inside the Saint-Euverte salon she is dropped, and the grudging non-invitation puts her outside. The narrator ironizes the hostess's winnowing of «réprouvés» rather than endorsing her verdict.

status_effects.explanation: He is thoroughly ridiculed as ignorant, philistine, and vain about his name in the death notices, down to misusing an idiom he does not understand.
Her rank is registered inside the scene by a whole avenue of guests who know they will never be admitted to her acquaintance and treat the mere sight of her as a public spectacle.
Society's own conduct is reported against her: her guests attend under obligation, her salon is fled rather than sought, and her supposed preeminence is placed near the bottom of Paris.
She crosses from inside the Saint-Euverte salon to outside it: dropped from the invitation list, and the intercession on her behalf yields only a refusal disguised as permission.

ambiguities: «la vieille Mme de Cambremer» is read here as the dowager marquise rather than Mme de Cambremer née Legrandin; the reference sheet leaves the bare surface form ambiguous between the two, and only the epithet «vieille» and the Franquetot cousinship support the reading.

The Saint-Euverte movement is double-edged: the passage grants that she really did transform her salon and that the printed guest lists are not false, while insisting that the standing so acquired is illusory. The negative verdict is dominant but rests on the narrator's distinction between real and publicized elegance.
